terra.problem: The joke about tripping over Paul's two uses of “but” makes the way Scripture is written the joke, and its tray image does not make sense.
The drawer callback does not explain that Papa Dorin was in a drawer, so a baker unfamiliar with his story lacks the context.
Saying Paul puts his hope in the raising attributes a feeling to him that this passage does not state.
Saying the joining leaves a mark implies an effect the passage does not specify.
Saying the joining does not come and go without a trace implies a lasting effect the passage does not specify.
The passage does not say whether money can buy closeness with the Lord.
The closing-sale joke suggests Papa Dorin was paid, whereas Mother Miller paid a quarter to buy him. The joke also lacks enough backstory to make sense.
This calls the subject heavy after either explanation on stop 2, card 2 has already done so. He can say that once.
This calls the subject heavy after either explanation on stop 2, card 2 has already done so. He can say that once.
The keys joke does not follow: a body is not a place people normally keep keys.
The handle joke does not make sense: Papa Dorin is a cookie stamper, so his handle is part of a tool.
The passage says the Holy Spirit was received from God, but does not say the believers did not earn Him.
The clearance-shelf joke treats the Holy Spirit like merchandise, making a holy subject the joke.
Comparing keeping one's body to hoarding a cookie suggests that not being one's own means not withholding one's body. That is not what Paul says.
The cookie-hoarding comparison does not match Paul's point about glorifying God with the body.
